design_notes: Checked against raw files and found correct (no finding): CHGCAR grid order (x fastest, reshaped (nz,ny,nx) then transposed). Confirmed on the non-cubic 48x96x216 alloy AECCAR0: core density at atom sites has median 1.8e5, against 0.064 when read x-slowest; the arsenic AECCAR0 maximum is at the As site (40,40,40).

Checked: the CHGCAR grid mean equals NELECT (256.99998 against 257 for As; 126.0, 96.0, 8.0, 48.0, 176.0 elsewhere). The magnetization block integrates to OSZICAR mag= (0.00056 against 0.0006; -0.25 against -0.25). In spin-polarized D2, D3 and alloy runs, CHGCAR, ELFCAR and LOCPOT each hold 2 blocks and the AECCAR files 1. Every grid matches the census grid_* fields. The rescan past the per-ion magnetic-moment line before the second block works.

Checked: the occupancy-walk gap reproduces census eig_gap within 1e-3 on all 5,010 runs that have a census gap (0 mismatches). Read_Eigenvalues k-point and band counts match eig_nk/eig_nb on all 5,010; spin count matches o_ispin; NELECT matches o_nelect; weights sum to 1 within 3e-7.

Checked: Read_Geometry on all 10,148 POSCAR/CONTCAR files gives no errors. Species and counts match census p_species/p_counts, and the cell volume matches p_volume, including every POSCAR with a negative (target-volume) scale. All files are Direct; none uses a three-component scale line or omits the species line (VASP 4 format).

Checked: the on-disk electron_count equals census o_nelect on 5,066 of 5,066 archives, final_magnetization equals osz_mag on 1,969 of 1,969, and per-atom species match the census on 5,084 of 5,085. The exception is the stray H2 run 'diamond', where the census has no species. Fresh Extract_Run output is identical to the on-disk archives for the arsenic run and the alloy 1-x-0 run.

The plan says to rebuild the density of states from 'EIGENVAL + IBZKPT weights'. The code uses the EIGENVAL weights, which equal the normalized IBZKPT weights. The two are equivalent, so this is not reported.

SMEARING_WIDTH_BY_CAMPAIGN gives relaxation_pool 0.2 eV. The plan sets no width for the Relaxation Pool, and only says that below about 50 irreducible k-points the smearing must be wide. The table has no alloy_ensemble entry, so State_Density_Of_Archive would raise KeyError if an alloy curve block were ever added. Neither is a contradiction today.
Read_Outcar_Echoes takes split()[2] of the first line containing 'NELECT'. A VASP build that echoes an INCAR 'NELECT=...' line without spaces would break this; no corpus OUTCAR does.
Read_Final_Magnetization reads only the first component after 'mag='. A noncollinear run prints three; none is in the corpus.

Freshness_Of_Store caches the report on the census file's size and mtime only. Rebuilding archives without touching the census leaves a stale cached report in a long-lived process. The code is in store.py, outside this slice.
could_not_check: A full OUTCAR sweep (12.0 GB over 5,085 files) comparing TITEL line count with species count, and counting NELECT lines, on every run. Only 19 runs (TITEL) and 400 runs (NELECT) were sampled. Exact computation: for each census row with an OUTCAR, count lines containing 'TITEL' and compare with len(p_species); count lines containing 'NELECT'.

A full volumetric sweep comparing mean(charge_density)*cell_volume with electron_count, and the magnetization_density integral with final_magnetization, for every archive. It needs about 8 GB of float32 reads across 547 full-field runs plus the density-only campaigns. 12 runs across all corpora were checked by hand. Exact computation: for each archive with charge_density, abs(mean(charge_density)*cell_volume - electron_count) < 1e-3, and for each with magnetization_density, abs(mean*V - final_magnetization) < 1e-3.

Whether VASP 6.2's ELFCAR second block is spin-down ELF and LOCPOT's second block is the spin-down potential, rather than some other combination, could not be checked against the VASP source or wiki (the web is off-limits). The data agree with up and down: both LOCPOT blocks are full potentials (-13.174 and -13.180 eV means), not a near-zero difference.

design_notes: Under the test suite the salted floor's interquartile range of 11.58 over 21 unit medians means at least 6 of 21 units score above about 11.6 normalized MAE. 'a handful ... badly conditioned ... most plausibly a rare-element shell fit' is untested speculation. A competing explanation: superposed_atomic_density peaks at 1,400-8,200 e/A^3 at nuclei (an all-electron-like atomic superposition), while charge_density peaks at about 2-3 e/A^3, so the ridge target rho - SAD carries core spikes of about -1000. Only 6% of the superposed-density floor's own error comes from those 64 core voxels, so the superposed-density floor itself is not dominated by them.

Gate b is set against a floor median whose upper quartile is about 100x the median. A 3x-of-median bar (0.037) is well defined, but the floor is broken on over a quarter of the block, so 'beats the reduced-salted floor' is weak evidence.

DeepDft.__call__ does not resolve species through SpeciesKeys. A caller passing an unseen (element, title) pair gets AtomEmbedding's ValueError rather than the unknown row. Every current caller (report.py, Cached_Structure) resolves first.

Renormalized_To_Electron_Count divides by the predicted density integral with no guard. On the untrained demonstration the integral is 0.88 electrons for a 261-electron target, so the scale is about 300x and negative densities scale too (renormalized min -2.47). This is harmless for a trained model but unguarded.

The task card structure_to_charge_defects lists metrics (normalized_mean_absolute_error, relative_l2) and the covariate pseudopotential_titles. report.py computes the floors in normalized MAE only and reports no relative L2 floor or per-title breakdown.

Held-out chemistry is tested by element only, while the vocabulary is keyed by (element, title). A fold-zero run with a known element under a new title would route to the unknown row yet be tagged interpolation. No element has two titles in this campaign today (check1.py).
The comment at report.py lines 85-86 (fold-one early stopping) sits above DEEP_DFT_SEED instead of LoadedBlock. This is cosmetic.

Test_Probes_Never_Send re-implements the role filter inside the test rather than exercising MessagePassingStack, so it would pass even if message_passing.py stopped filtering. Test_Probes_Never_Influence_Atom_Features does cover the real path indirectly.

That computation would give the per-unit errors (to name the units above 11.6 normalized MAE) and the floor values after correcting the Si-impurity species label. Exact computation: block=LoadedBlock(); Measured_Floors(block) with Species_Keys_Of fixed for 34c5ebd36d43713f/bd39ceefa779d83c, then compare salted_errors and copy_errors per unit.
The member is untrained (no /Pool/VASP_DATA/_derived/_training/deep_dft/ directory exists), so no gate verdict, curve or checkpoint could be checked.

Whether the AECCAR1-derived superposed_atomic_density is the right reference for a pseudo-valence charge_density floor belongs to the data/floors slice. Only the peak-magnitude comparison above was checked.

design_notes: One-dimensional strain arms exclude the zero-strain reference run (family 'reference'), so the levels at +/-0.005 are bracketed across a 0.010 gap that skips a real calculation at zero strain; the two-angle shear grid likewise lacks (0,0). Including the reference as a level of every arm would tighten those brackets.

Isotropic levels interpolate linearly in cell volume (the Vol_ number), while the member's input is the isotropic strain; the floor and the member therefore use different parameterizations of the same sweep (volume is cubic in strain).

The perovskite length arm lacks the (1,1,1) center (excluded as the byte duplicate of the angle arm's center, exclusion E3), which removes 9 of its 27 potential interior levels (18 left); the angle arm's identical center could serve both arms.

Canon section 9.6 names 'POD + k-nearest-neighbor interpolation (the memorization null)' as a floor; the parametric block builds a 1-nearest full-field copy and a ridge onto a rank-32 POD instead. The 1-NN copy is the k=1 limit, so this is a narrowing rather than a contradiction.

Bracket_Corners refuses brackets next to a hole rather than widening to the next available values; this is conservative and documented, but it is why three-angle shear keeps only 20 of 64 interior grid positions.

The kill bar uses the pooled median over levels, which is dominated by triaxial (216 of 423 levels); a run-weighted pooled median of the per-run floor is 0.025%, a level-weighted one 0.091% - the choice of weighting moves the bar by almost 4x and is not discussed.
could_not_check: Whether a trained parametric member would pass or fail: no parametric training run exists under /Pool/VASP_DATA/_derived/_training/factorized_fourier/ (nothing matching 'param').

Re-running the full ridge/nearest/mean floors on a per-run, per-functional, per-plane population (would need ~2,358 40-cubed fields, ~1.2 GB, plus POD; borderline on the memory limit): compute Strain_Ridge_Nearest_Mean_Floor_Rows with each run as its own row, its own tensor as input, and compare medians with report.md.

A leave-one-arm-out block as the canon specifies (hold out each strain family in turn, fit ridge/nearest/mean on the other six, score the held-out family per run) was not computed; it would show whether the 0.064% bar survives the canon's own split.

design_notes: The grid-transfer bar cannot measure transfer as built: Trained_Manifold_Member trains point-sampled on every grid shape (train role: 1216 runs at 40^3 and 640 on 14 other shapes), so the off-dominant test shapes were all seen in training; the off-dominant shapes may also correlate with strain family, which the ratio does not separate (not checked). A transfer test would train on 40^3 only.

The radial-basis, ridge and copy floors are fit on the 524 non-interior (boundary) levels and asked to predict all 423 interior levels, while the bracketing floor uses each level's immediate neighbours; the two kill floors are therefore very different tasks (the RBF is nearly an extrapolation from the arm's boundary shell).

The 1.5-hour run cap in IMPLEMENTATION.md and the report.py comment ('sized against the entry's 1.5-hour card cap') is not in test-suite.md II.3 and nothing in the code enforces it; the source of the cap is not recorded.

Manifold_Member_Arm_Predictions averages the member's predictions at both functional features against the level's mean over both functionals; this matches the truth construction because every interior level carries equal numbers of cheap and accurate runs (357 levels 1+1, 66 levels 3+3), but the code does not check it.

Verified correct: parameter count 272,001 (branch 100,736 + decoder 171,265); PeriodicCoordinateFeatures(4) is 25 wide; the committed floor medians (0.000911, 0.000991, 0.004225, 0.019876) reproduce from Host_Floors; test split is 248 runs / 30 units, 176 runs / 22 units at 40^3, 72 runs on eight other shapes (all 36/48-axis); improvement figures -169.2%, -147.4%, -31.56% follow from results.json medians; the 19-figure count matches figures/pooled; the slice test file passes (11) and test_imports passes (10), matching commit 43715fb's '21 tests'; training curves hold 200 + 3000 + 3000 + 4000 steps.

Computation: load manifold_stage2 parameters, call Manifold_Member_Arm_Predictions restricted to the 47 test-role interior levels, with unit_key set to each level's orbit and shear levels keyed by plane, then Compare_To_Floor against the same-population bracketing and RBF floors.
Whether renormalizing predictions to the electron count (the card's conservation law) changes the committed headline 0.002424 or the transfer ratio: requires evaluating the trained member.

The results page's '≈0.7 GB sampled', 'seven minutes on the card' and '46 minutes' figures: no persisted artifact records them (the peak is never written and the stage manifests were overwritten by a zero-step CPU resume); checkpoint mtimes 10:25-10:32 are consistent with about seven minutes of training.
Whether a rerun of Main reproduces report.md exactly (resume returns checkpointed parameters; bootstrap seeding not traced) was not tested, since running the report generator is forbidden.

design_notes: Weak floors. The V-read bar (0.335752) is 30% under hartree_plus_semilocal_xc_ridge (0.479646 mean-removed relative L2 on fold 0). On the same fold, factorized_fourier/report.md lists stronger floors: hartree_plus_climatology 0.403326, per_shell_linear_filter 0.282422 and training_mean_trivial_floor 0.184317. A member could clear the V-read bar while losing to the training-mean template. Likewise the K2 ELF bar (0.078094) is about 5x looser than the template floor (0.015957). Adding those floors, as the flagship did, would make the bars meaningful.

The K3 low-data slice is drawn per run identifier rather than per split unit, so a PBE/HSE pair or a config/sigma re-run of one defect can be split between in-slice and out-of-slice. That causes no leak, since the slice lives inside the training folds, but the 'quarter' counts near-duplicate re-runs separately.

The masked loss weights every hidden token equally in transformed space. ELF tokens (range 0 to 1) contribute about 1e-2 per voxel, while standardized magnetization in magnetic runs contributes about 1e1 to 1e4, so the pretrain objective is dominated by magnetization and density rather than by the ELF and potential reads the kills judge.

V.1 says 'learned-Fourier variable encodings'. VariableEncoding adds a constant learned vector per label (label_encodings shape (6, 32)) with no spatial or Fourier dependence. IMPLEMENTATION.md does not say whether this is the intended reading.

Pretrain_Step_Count sets the six-hour budget from the cost probe's 2.2917 s/step, which includes only one validation pass per 300 steps. The staged run validates every 100 steps (about 32 s per pass, inferred from the 200-step probe's 469 s against the 300-step probe's 687.5 s) and adds a 200-step divergence probe outside the 9,425-step budget, so the 'six-hour' pretrain would run about 6.5 to 7 hours.

Test_The_Masked_Loss_Ignores_Visible_Tokens stubs Forward_Tokens, so no test checks the leakage property that matters most: changing a hidden channel's ground truth must not change the forward output. By construction (full*visible + flag*(1-visible)) it holds today, but nothing guards it.

No driver or report code builds V.1's 'full any-to-any completion matrix' deliverable, or the alloy zero-shot evaluation path. Since the member was never judged, these are open items rather than defects.

How far the stopped pretrain got (completed steps, best validation) is stored only inside completion_fold0_pretrain_20260916_stage0_checkpoint.npz, which this audit may not open. The computation needed is: read 'completed_steps' and the validation arrays from that npz with numpy and compare them with Staged_Step_Counts(9425) = (2828, 2828, 3769).

design_notes: Checked and found correct: in-house Adam matches torch.optim.Adam to 2.8e-17 over 50 steps; numpy and torch transforms agree to ~1e-14 (both unnormalized forward, 1/N inverse); real and complex round trips exact on both engines; GELU tanh form matches torch gelu(approximate='tanh') to 2e-16 and its derivative matches autograd to 1e-15; sqrt(2/pi) constant correct; Reciprocal_Rows satisfies A B^T = 2 pi I; Periodic_Convolution_3d's flip makes conv3d equal the roll-and-accumulate sum for odd stencils; vector-Jacobian product on both engines equals the closed form 2 A^T (c * Ax); Recomputed_In_Backward gives gradients identical to the plain call through closed-over weights; commit 82d0b59's numbers (4.8e-9, 35.69 = two-thirds, 3.7e-9, exact foreign match) reproduce.

Softplus differs between engines by up to 1.9e-9 just above 20, because torch's softplus switches to the identity past threshold=20 while numpy uses logaddexp exactly; harmless at reported precision but an engine disagreement the conformance rows do not probe.

NumpyEngine's step of 1e-6 is only exact for float64 parameters: on a float32 parameter near 1 the stored perturbation rounds to about 9.5e-7, a ~5% gradient error. ParameterSet is typed float64 so this is not reachable through typed callers.

Centered_Modes assigns the even-extent Nyquist index to +N/2 (numpy fftfreq gives -N/2). For the floors' spectral Laplacian on skewed cells the multiplier is then not Hermitian on Nyquist planes, but taking the real part reproduces the symmetric trigonometric interpolant's Laplacian at grid points, so I judge it correct; a docstring naming the convention would help.

Reset_Peak_Accelerator_Bytes / Peak_Accelerator_Bytes report torch's allocated (not reserved) bytes on the current device only; 'held' in the docstring could be read as reserved memory. Recorded cost-probe peaks therefore understate what the card actually holds.

The test plan's in-house gate ('no external deep-learning frameworks') is departed from by design (torch autograd and torch.fft behind the seam); the reason is recorded in operators/README.md 'The substrate seams', so I did not file it as a silent deviation, only the stale 'decision open' line.

Several substrate comments state reasons rather than mechanics (engine.py 'central differences at a step of 1e-6 cancel six digits...', torch_engine.py 'without the annotation inference widens the literal...', operations.py 'the tanh form, so every engine returns the same numbers'), against the README's comment register; filed only the fourier.py block.

Engine is a Protocol but NumpyEngine and TorchEngine do not inherit it by name, unlike the README's stated pattern for Operator, Kernel and Composition; the README restricts that rule to those three, so not filed.
could_not_check: Whether any production call path ever hands Periodic_Convolution_3d, Contract_Channel_Axis, Einstein_Summation or CustomGradient.Apply a mix of numpy and foreign arrays at runtime: would need instrumenting a training step of each member (not run, as training drivers are off-limits).

Peak_Accelerator_Bytes behavior on the card: CUDA was hidden for this audit (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=), so the accelerator paths (device placement, peak counter, Host_Array from the card) were only read, not executed.

design_notes: Augmentation and the equivariance error do not need the operations to be crystal symmetries: any signed permutation plus whole-voxel shift is an isometry of a cubic periodic cell, so the wrong glide on the 64-atom grids changes no reported number; it only makes the 'exact symmetry' wording and the quarter-divisibility gate wrong. The real hazards are non-cubic lattices (primitive, strained) and lattice conditioning that is not transformed with the field.

test-suite 9.5(a) says 'Train on Fourier-truncated 40-cubed inputs ... evaluate at 80-cubed'; Resolution_Axis evaluates the operator on the coarse input and asks for an 80-cubed output, rather than handing it the fine input. Both readings are defensible; the README phrase 'train coarse, evaluate fine' does not say which.

README calls the uniform-grid weight 'cell volume / point count ... exactly the /V_cell normalization the data pipeline already performs'. The two are distinct steps (the store holds electrons per cubic angstrom, and the weight multiplies by V/N on top: sum(rho)*V/N = 255.99995 against 256 electrons for 049d8f7daec846ab); the sentence is loose rather than demonstrably wrong.

Quadrature_Weights trusts quadrature.point_count and never checks it against the grid it weights; the test ResamplingOperator returns a GridFunction on a new grid carrying the old quadrature. No production misuse found (every production site rebuilds UniformGridQuadrature from the output point count).
The symmetry median includes the identity operation (error exactly 0), which biases the median slightly low.
Galerkin attention has no Dense_Reference_Integral test, but Test_Galerkin_Attention_Matches_The_Explicit_Pairwise_Form_At_Four_Cubed plays that role, so README rule 2 is met in substance.
could_not_check: Whether the stopped codomain-attention pretrain checkpoint (completion_fold0_pretrain_20260916_stage0) is materially affected by its augmentation; that would need loading the checkpoint, which this audit forbids. By the isometry argument the field augmentation itself is physically valid for that lattice-blind member.

A sweep of the symmetry operations over every pristine 64-atom run (only one 80-cubed density and two 40-cubed ELF fields were checked); computation: for every supercell_strains run with a cubic lattice, the relative change under each of the 48 operations as written and with the translation halved.

design_notes: Byte determinism verified across processes, not just within the test's one process: re-rendering the cached inspection.npz for nonlinear_manifold_decoder (17 figures), residual_correction (22) and alias_free_convolutional (27) into scratch produced byte-identical PNGs to the committed ones (rerender.py in the scratch folder). No finding.

Rank-3 per-axis Fourier mode weights (39, 64, 64) = (modes, in, out) go to Render_Field_Slices, which draws 'axis k center' slices with an auto-scaled viridis map. That is honest but reads a weight tensor as a volume and never centers signed weights on zero. A Render_Matrix sheet per mode might read better.

Orbit_Summary's per-family orbit counts sum to 300 while the 'all' row gives 296: four one-angle-shear orbits (e.g. +0.0250 xy) are also two-angle-shear orbits. The table is correct as sets but invites a wrong sum; a note or an 'orbits shared with another family' column would help.

The README and test-suite.md say 'roughly 299' / '~299 exchangeable orbit units'; the orbit map measures 296 and test_inspection hard-codes 296. 'Roughly' covers it, but the canon could state the measured number.

British spellings in the inspection layer (Centred_On_Zero, 'centred', 'colour', 'colours', 'centre', test name ..._Colour_Scale). The only in-repo rule ('American English everywhere') is in 1-archive/journals/practice/conventions.md, which is archived, so I did not file this as a contradiction.

Describe_Run returns the full sidecar, including pseudopotential_titles. It is in-memory only, but any caller that writes the description into a report would export license-derived strings. Consider dropping that key in the catalog view.
Render_Table takes its columns from the first row: extra keys in later rows are silently dropped and missing keys raise KeyError. No current caller mixes row shapes, as far as I checked.

The two-branch floors figure draws the density-alone twin as a bar under the legend label 'floor'; the twin is a comparator, not a floor. The figure also omits three of the five floors the report tabulates (per_shell_filter, training_mean_trivial, nearest_run_copy).

Render_Field_Slices draws without the constant-array guard and with a sequential map even for signed fields, unlike Render_Matrix and Render_Field_Sheet. The three renderers are inconsistent about diverging maps.
test_inspection.py passes in full (12 tests, including the two pool-marked ones). pyright strict is clean on operators/inspection and the test file.
could_not_check: Commit 7961b5b's 'On the assembled member it writes twelve figures and skips nothing': needs the member's Inspect() at that commit, i.e. constructing and running the 2026-09-06 assembly. Not attempted.

Whether the galerkin_transformer and gaussian_plane_wave reports render inspection suites at all: their report.py files do not call Render_Inspection_Suite. They are outside this slice and were not audited against the inspection doctrine.

Whether every rank-4 array any member's Inspect() can emit is stack-first. Only the cached inspection.npz archives on /Pool were surveyed (the 4 channel-last keys found). design_notes: The perovskite nearest_angle_copy floor (Perovskite_Nearest_Neighbor_Predictions and the Galerkin report's own copy) measures distance in raw factor space and ignores the exact angle-permutation symmetry: a symmetry-aware copy reaches median relative L2 about 1.8e-7 on fold 0 versus 0.0853 for the built copy, so the memorization null is far weaker than the plan's 'brutal on factorial sweeps' intent. Follows from the fold-map leak reported as a finding.

Identity_And_Affine_Floors (and residual_correction's Affine_Predictions) fit the affine map per pair on the evaluated pair's own accurate field, i.e. an oracle in-sample fit, not one global map fitted on training pairs; the docstring is honest ('per-pair'), but the name 'global affine' in test-suite 9.6 and the reports suggests a single fitted map.

Scissor_Floor fits the linear scissor in-sample over all 1340 strain pairs, including the 160 auxiliary rotational-copy points and byte-alias duplicates (test-suite IV.1 says 'all 1,339 pairs'); it is reported as context, but its residual is not an orbit-held-out number.

test-suite 9.6 names 'POD + k-nearest-neighbor interpolation' as the memorization null; every member builds a 1-NN field copy (Nearest_Training_Run) with no POD and no interpolation. II.1 itself asks for a '1-NN field copy', so the plan is internally inconsistent rather than the code deviating.

Shell_Index_Grid uses integer mode radius with no lattice metric; isotropic in physical wavevector only on cubic cells. It is used only on the cubic 64-atom block, so no number is affected, but it would be anisotropic on the fcc primitive strain cells.

Frequency_Split_Relative_L2 (operators/metrics) sums squared rfftn coefficients without doubling the non-self-conjugate modes, so its band errors are not the Parseval-weighted relative L2 of each band; affects every frequency-split number including PerovskiteAngleBlock.Scored. Outside my files; worth its own check.

Perovskite floors (ridge, copy, training mean) are scored without the card's renormalization while the DeepONet member is renormalized; copies are true fields (48 electrons) so only the ridge and mean floors are affected, and relative L2 is not scale-invariant, so the floor and member are scored under different post-processing.

Write_Member_Results would emit non-standard JSON (NaN) for a NaN metric; Read_Member_Results(Write_Member_Results(x)) == x only for values already at six decimals, so Test_Member_Results_Round_Trip_Through_Json only checks clean decimals.

Test_The_Results_Page_Headlines_Match_The_Member_Artifacts accepts a headline if it equals any row median of the member at the printed precision, regardless of group or metric, and skips every entry whose member has no results.json (I.1, I.3, II.1, II.4, VI.1), so it cannot catch a wrong headline for any passing member.

The cross-member table shows the residual_correction ceiling and context floors as 'identity:pass' against a 0% bar, the same label as the member's kill-bar pass; the table drops required_improvement, so a context comparison and a canon kill read the same.
The residual_correction conformal row reports the median of per-orbit coverage (1.000000) while the results page quotes coverage 0.977; a median of a coverage indicator is not the coverage statistic.

perovskite_block.py comment says 'every one of the 249 perovskite runs integrates to exactly this'; the store holds 250 archives and all 250 integrate to 48.0 within 1.6e-6 (249 is the distinct count), so the comment is right only as distinct runs.

The Galerkin report renormalizes each prediction to 'that truth's own electron count' (computed from the evaluated truth) rather than the card's known 48.0; numerically identical here but it reads the truth at inference.
could_not_check: Effect of the perovskite fold-map leak on the DeepONet lattice_to_charge verdicts: needs regenerating perovskite_folds.json grouped by the 35 permutation orbits and retraining/re-evaluating the fold-0 and holdout members (training run, not allowed here).

Whether factorized_fourier and deep_operator_network report numbers would pass the cross-member signature check against the members already in the table: needs their results.json, which only running their report generators would write.
The Stage-0 floor numbers in operators/stage0-report.md were not recomputed (python -m operators.data.stage0 is a report generator); I checked only the floor functions it calls.

design_notes: operators/pyproject.toml calls torch optional, but operators/training/hardware.py Training_Engine always returns TorchEngine, so every training driver and trained-member report needs torch. Torch is optional only for importing the package and running the numpy reference paths.

operators/deep_operator_network/configs/canonical.toml says report.py's constants are what was measured, 'same as the other three configs in this directory'. Of those three, only energy_trunk.toml carries such a note; proper_orthogonal.toml and principal_component.toml state stale values with no caveat. No code reads any of the four TOML files (grep finds no reader in operators/deep_operator_network).

operators/alias_free_convolutional/manifest.toml lists kernels = ["compact_support", "spectral"]. The member assembles only TabulatedStencilKernel; any spectral dependence is transitive, through operators.factorized_fourier helpers and spectral resampling, not a kernel from operators.kernels.spectral.

The cubic block mixes cubic defect_set cells with strained supercell_strains cells (87 of 196 training runs non-cubic), so the name 'cubic block' and Apply_Grid_Operation's 'compatible cubic grid' precondition are both loosely met.
The AliasFreeConvolutional class docstring says 'a multi-scale stack of alias-free convolutional layers' even when the class is built as the pointwise twin.

STENCIL_HALF_WIDTHS fixes one voxel per axis at every scale, so the stencil's physical reach doubles at each coarser scale. test-suite.md I.2's gate wording is 'convolutions of fixed physical support'.
